title: Incident #105: ETS Session Wipeout When Cache Worker Crashes
solutionExplanation: Adds {heir, HeirPid, keep_alive} to ets:new/2 options and implements ets:give_away/3 in transfer_to_restarted_worker to safely preserve session tables across worker crashes.

otpDocCards.description: Changes the owner of table Tab to Pid. The new owner receives an {'ETS-TRANSFER', Tab, FromPid, GiftData} message.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) pointer transfer in the ETS registry.

mentalModelCheck.question: When an owning worker crashes, what message does the designated heir process receive in its mailbox from ERTS?

options.label: {'EXIT', WorkerPid, killed}
options.explanation: Exit signals are sent to linked processes when trapping exits, not the ETS transfer message.

options.label: {'ETS-TRANSFER', TableId, DeadOwnerPid, HeirData}
options.explanation: ERTS automatically delivers {'ETS-TRANSFER', TableId, DeadOwnerPid, HeirData} to the heir process mailbox, transferring legal ownership without deleting table rows.

options.label: {reclaim_cache, TableId}
options.explanation: This is not an ERTS system message.

options.label: {'DOWN', Ref, process, WorkerPid, crash}
options.explanation: DOWN messages are sent by process monitors, not the ETS heir mechanism.

incidentAlert.symptom: Every time a malformed request crashes the session_cache worker, all 250,000 logged-in users are simultaneously logged out and forced to re-authenticate!
incidentAlert.rootCauseHint: create_session_table/1 calls ets:new(incident_sessions_tab, [set, public, named_table]) without a {heir, HeirPid, keep_alive} option, and transfer_to_restarted_worker/2 fails to call ets:give_away/3.
incidentAlert.fixObjective: Add {heir, HeirPid, keep_alive} to ets:new/2 in create_session_table/1 and implement ets:give_away(Tab, NewWorkerPid, keep_alive) in transfer_to_restarted_worker/2.
